content: This information does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or suitable for your use. It is not intended to replace individualized medical advice and should not substitute for the guidance of your healthcare professional. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. How to Use: This medication is administered by injection into a vein or muscle as directed by your doctor, typically 1 to 3 times daily. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition and response to treatment. Before use, visually inspect the product for particles or discoloration; do not use the liquid if either is present. For optimal effectiveness, use this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. Continue using the medication for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Side Effects: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or headache may occur. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Prolonged or repeated use may lead to oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a comprehensive list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for guidance. Precautions: Before using lincomycin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, clindamycin, or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients (e.g., benzyl alcohol) that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Lincomycin may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines (e.g., typhoid vaccine). During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. It is known to pass into breast milk. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all products you use (including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Notes: Laboratory and medical tests (e.g., kidney/liver function, blood counts) may be conducted while you are using this medication. Keep all medical and lab appointments. Consult your doctor for further details. Missed Dose: It is important to take each dose of this medication as scheduled. If you miss a dose, contact your doctor or pharmacist immediately for a new dosing schedule. Storage: Refer to the product instructions and consult your pharmacist for proper storage details. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Information: This summary does not include all possible details about this product. Always seek complete information from your healthcare provider regarding this product and your specific health needs.
